---
title: "What is the best lift-to-drag ratio, and at what angle of attack?"
---


::: {#9d257c80 .cell execution_count=2}
``` {.python .cell-code}
ENTRY_CEILING = 60.0
SOLVE_BUDGET = 15.0
PROBE_POOL = 150.0
PROBE_SPENT = 5.6

import aerosandbox as asb
import aerosandbox.numpy as np

alphas = np.linspace(0, 12, 61)
airplane = get_airplane()
op_point = asb.OperatingPoint(velocity=5.0, alpha=alphas)
aero = asb.AeroBuildup(airplane=airplane, op_point=op_point).run()

LD = aero['L'] / aero['D']
best_idx = np.argmax(LD)
max_LD = LD[best_idx]
best_alpha = alphas[best_idx]
```
:::


::: {.hero}
[5\.38]{.hero-value}
[Best L/D]{.hero-label}
:::

**Answer.** The X-Wing achieves a maximum lift-to-drag ratio of [5\.38]{.key} at an angle of attack of [6\.0°]{.key}.

::: {.callout-note}
## New assumptions
1. **velocity: 5 m/s**, typical for a chuck glider.
:::

::: {#cell-fig-ld-vs-alpha .cell execution_count=3}
``` {.python .cell-code}
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import aerosandbox.tools.pretty_plots as p

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5, 4))
ax.plot(alphas, LD)
ax.axvline(best_alpha, color="k", linestyle="--", alpha=0.5)
ax.set_xlabel(r"Angle of attack $\alpha$ [deg]")
ax.set_ylabel(r"Lift-to-drag ratio $L/D$")
ax.set_title("X-Wing Lift-to-Drag Ratio")
p.show_plot()
```
